heuristics.name: most typical collocation
heuristics.description: Picked the option whose most common collocation (benign tumor, redacted document, perishable goods, draconian rules) seemed the likeliest sentence the item was built around.

heuristics.name: classic test-word
heuristics.description: When collocations tied, picked the option that is a canonical ISEE/SSAT vocabulary word (malingered, surreptitious, mercurial).

heuristics.name: two-blank internal coherence
heuristics.description: For two-blank items, picked the pair whose halves are logically linked (lucid->summarize, growing->afford, stability->unchanged) or form a canonical contrast (austere/lavish, brief/thorough).

notes: Single-blank sets share part of speech and register; distractors are as rare as plausible keys, so no reliable option-only tell. Two-blank items were the only ones with any internal structure, and even there every pair was internally sensible. All picks marked guess; no reject marked certain.
